entities.summary: Ulrich Beck was a German sociologist, and one of the most cited social scientists in the world during his lifetime. His work focused on questions of uncontrollability, ignorance and uncertainty in the modern age, and he coined the terms "risk society" and "second modernity" or "reflexive modernization". He also tried to overturn national perspectives that predominated in sociological investigations with a cosmopolitanism that acknowledges the interconnectedness of the modern world. He was a professor at the University of Munich and also held appointments at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l’Homme (FMSH) in Paris, and at the London School of Economics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ulrich Beck's work on 'risk society' and 'second modernity' influenced sociological thought by highlighting the interconnectedness of global issues and the need for a cosmopolitan perspective. His ideas have had significant regional impact, particularly in Europe and beyond.
